record.paper_title: Some open questions and conjectures about visibility and iteration in bounded convex domains in ℂ^N
record.original_question: Can there exist a bounded convex domain Ω ⊂ ℂ^N that is not visible, but for which every geodesic ray γ:[0,+∞)→Ω has a landing point in the Euclidean boundary, meaning that lim_{t→∞} γ(t) exists?

evidence.quote: Question 3.10. Does there exist a bounded convex domain Ω which is not visible and such that all geodesic rays land?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $N\geq 1$ and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^N$ be a bounded convex domain, equipped with its Kobayashi distance $k_\Omega$. A geodesic ray is a map $\gamma:[0,+\infty)\to\Omega$ such that $k_\Omega(\gamma(s),\gamma(t))=|t-s|$ for all $s,t\geq 0$. We say that $\gamma$ lands at a point $p$ in the Euclidean boundary $\partial\Omega$ if $\lim_{t\to+\infty}\gamma(t)=p$ exists in $\mathbb{C}^N$.

The domain $\Omega$ is said to be visible if for every pair of distinct points $p,q\in\partial\Omega$ and every pair of sequences $(x_n),(y_n)\subset\Omega$ with $x_n\to p$ and $y_n\to q$, there exist a compact set $K\subset\Omega$ and Kobayashi geodesic segments $\sigma_n$ joining $x_n$ to $y_n$ such that $\sigma_n\cap K\neq\emptyset$ for all sufficiently large $n$.

Question: Does there exist a bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}^N$ which is not visible, yet such that every geodesic ray $\gamma:[0,+\infty)\to\Omega$ lands at some point of $\partial\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open question in a 2025 list of open problems on visibility in bounded convex domains. Related work studies non-visibility and the geometry of cluster sets of Kobayashi geodesics, but no source found resolves the existence of a non-visible bounded convex domain in which all geodesic rays land.

status_evidence.title: On non-visibility of Kobayashi geodesics and the geometry of the boundary
status_evidence.snippet: Limit sets of non-visible Kobayashi geodesics are contained in a complex face of the boundary.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on non-visible geodesics, but no resolution of the landing question.
